title: Identity for AVD: Entra Join Types, FSLogix Kerberos, and SSO
summary: Every AVD security decision starts with one question: what identity backs your session hosts? This lesson maps the three supported join types — Microsoft Entra joined, Microsoft Entra hybrid joined, and Microsoft Entra Domain Services — to what they unlock and what they block, especially single sign-on. You'll learn why on-premises-only identities are never supported, how hybrid UPN/SID mismatches break sign-in, and how to wire FSLogix profile containers to Azure Files using Microsoft Entra Kerberos so profiles load without a domain controller in sight. You'll finish by enabling Microsoft Entra authentication for RDP — the mechanism behind AVD's recommended single sign-on experience — and know the licensing you need before you start.
objectives: Differentiate Microsoft Entra joined, Microsoft Entra hybrid joined, and Microsoft Entra Domain Services session hosts and identify which support Microsoft Entra single sign-on
Explain why AVD requires every user identity to be discoverable in Microsoft Entra ID, and apply the UPN/SID matching rule for hybrid identities
Configure FSLogix profile containers on Azure Files using Microsoft Entra Kerberos for hybrid, cloud-only, or external identities
List the licensing prerequisites for AVD access and Conditional Access-driven identity scenarios
Enable Microsoft Entra authentication for RDP and describe the five tasks required to turn on single sign-on for a host pool

quiz.q: Which session host join types are supported for Microsoft Entra single sign-on (SSO) to the session host itself?
options: Microsoft Entra Domain Services joined only
Active Directory Domain Services joined only, with no Microsoft Entra ID presence
Any join type, including standalone AD DS
Microsoft Entra joined or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined only
quiz.why: Session hosts must be Microsoft Entra joined or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined to use Entra SSO for RDP. Hosts joined only to Microsoft Entra Domain Services or only to AD DS aren't supported for this feature.

quiz.q: A hybrid AVD user's on-premises AD account is user@contoso.local, but their Microsoft Entra ID account is user@contoso.com. Under what condition does AVD support this configuration?
options: Only if either the UPN or the SID (ObjectSID / OnPremisesSecurityIdentifier) matches between the AD and Microsoft Entra ID accounts
It's never supported — UPNs must be identical across AD and Microsoft Entra ID
Only if the organization disables Microsoft Entra Connect synchronization
Only if the session host is Microsoft Entra Domain Services joined
quiz.why: AVD only supports mismatched UPNs when either the UPN or the SID for both the AD and Microsoft Entra ID accounts match — SID meaning the AD ObjectSID property matches the Microsoft Entra ID OnPremisesSecurityIdentifier property.

quiz.q: You're configuring Azure Files with Microsoft Entra Kerberos to host FSLogix profiles. What's true about the storage account's authentication method?
options: The storage account can authenticate with both Microsoft Entra ID and AD DS simultaneously for redundancy
The storage account can only use one authentication method at a time — Microsoft Entra ID, AD DS, or Microsoft Entra Domain Services, never two
Authentication method doesn't matter for FSLogix, only NTFS permissions do
Microsoft Entra Kerberos requires AD DS to also be enabled on the same account
quiz.why: An Azure Storage account can't authenticate with both Microsoft Entra ID and a second method like AD DS or Microsoft Entra Domain Services — only one authentication method can be active at a time.

quiz.q: Which Microsoft Entra application must have isRemoteDesktopProtocolEnabled set to true to enable Microsoft Entra authentication for RDP?
options: Azure Virtual Desktop
Microsoft Remote Desktop
Windows Cloud Login
Azure Virtual Desktop Azure Resource Manager Provider
quiz.why: You enable Microsoft Entra authentication for RDP by setting isRemoteDesktopProtocolEnabled to true on the Windows Cloud Login service principal (app ID 270efc09-cd0d-444b-a71f-39af4910ec45).

quiz.q: A session host is Microsoft Entra hybrid joined, and you're enabling Microsoft Entra SSO for RDP. What must you create first to avoid sign-in failures?
options: A second Azure Files share
A Windows Hello for Business certificate template
A Microsoft Entra Domain Services replica set
A Kerberos server object
quiz.why: Microsoft Entra hybrid joined session hosts need a Kerberos server object to complete authentication to a domain controller. Without it, connections may fail with a 'session doesn't exist' error or silently skip SSO.

quiz.q: In three to four sentences, explain why a session host joined only to Microsoft Entra Domain Services can't use Microsoft Entra single sign-on for RDP, and what identity model you'd recommend for a brand-new, cloud-only organization with no on-premises Active Directory.
quiz.answer: Microsoft Entra SSO for RDP depends on the session host itself having a Microsoft Entra device identity so it can receive an Entra-issued RDP access token; a host joined only to Microsoft Entra Domain Services is a member of a separate, Kerberos/NTLM-compatible managed domain and never establishes that Entra device identity, so the SSO token flow has nothing to attach to. For a greenfield, cloud-only organization, the recommended model is Microsoft Entra joined session hosts with cloud-only user identities, FSLogix profiles stored on Azure Files using Microsoft Entra Kerberos, and Microsoft Entra SSO enabled on the host pool — no AD DS or Microsoft Entra Domain Services required at all.
quiz.why: SSO requires the session host to hold a Microsoft Entra device identity, which Entra Domain Services and standalone AD DS joins don't provide. A cloud-only organization avoids the problem entirely by going fully Microsoft Entra joined, which is also the simplest identity model to operate.

body_markdown:
## Why Identity Comes Before Everything Else

Every AVD security decision in this module — RBAC, Conditional Access, session host hardening, Zero Trust — sits on top of one foundational choice: how are your session hosts and users identified? Get this wrong and you'll spend weeks debugging SSO failures, FSLogix profiles that won't mount, or Conditional Access policies that silently don't apply. Get it right and the rest of AVD security nearly falls into place.

## Three Ways to Join a Session Host

AVD supports three session host join configurations, and they aren't interchangeable:

| Join type | Cloud-only users | Hybrid users | Entra SSO for RDP | Needs DC line-of-sight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Microsoft Entra joined** | Yes | Yes (can be assigned to app groups) | Yes | No, unless you also need Kerberos to on-prem resources |
| **Microsoft Entra hybrid joined** | No | Yes | Yes | Yes for Kerberos, unless using Entra Kerberos for Azure Files |
| **Microsoft Entra Domain Services joined** | No (requires password hash sync) | Yes | **No** | Depends on your Entra Domain Services topology |

A fourth configuration — session hosts joined only to standalone AD DS with no Microsoft Entra ID presence at all — isn't supported: users must be discoverable through Microsoft Entra ID to access AVD, full stop.

The practical decision: greenfield, cloud-first deployments go Microsoft Entra joined. Estates with an existing on-premises AD DS footprint that must be preserved — line-of-business apps that need Kerberos or NTLM, GPO-managed tooling — go Microsoft Entra hybrid joined. Microsoft Entra Domain Services is a narrower option, useful when you want a lightweight managed domain without operating your own domain controllers, but it explicitly does not support Entra SSO for RDP. Plan around that limitation if SSO is a hard requirement.

## The Rule AVD Never Breaks

Whatever join type you choose, one rule never changes: AVD requires user identities to be discoverable through Microsoft Entra ID. Standalone Active Directory deployments — even ones federated through AD FS with no synchronization to Microsoft Entra ID — aren't supported. If you're migrating a legacy RDS estate that has never touched Entra ID, standing up Microsoft Entra Connect (or moving straight to cloud-only accounts) is a prerequisite, not an optional step.

## Hybrid Identity's Sharp Edge: UPN and SID Matching

Hybrid identities are common, but they carry a gotcha every AVD engineer eventually hits: a mismatch between the AD UPN and the Microsoft Entra ID UPN. If your on-premises account is `user@contoso.local` and it syncs to Microsoft Entra ID as `user@contoso.com`, AVD only supports that configuration if either the UPN **or** the SID matches between the two directories — where SID means the AD `ObjectSID` property matching the Microsoft Entra ID `OnPremisesSecurityIdentifier` property. When neither matches, users can authenticate to the AVD service but fail to sign in to the session host itself. This is one of the most common "SSO works for the portal but not the desktop" support tickets — check UPN/SID alignment before you touch anything else.

## FSLogix Profiles Without a Domain Controller

Traditionally, FSLogix profile containers on Azure Files needed AD DS or Microsoft Entra Domain Services for Kerberos authentication to the SMB share, which meant session hosts needed network line-of-sight to a domain controller at every logon. Microsoft Entra Kerberos removes that requirement: Microsoft Entra ID itself issues the Kerberos tickets needed to access the file share over standard SMB, and hybrid-joined or Entra-joined session hosts don't need DC line-of-sight to load a profile (a system with DC line-of-sight is still needed once, to configure share permissions).

The setup, in order:

1. Create the storage account and file share. A storage account can authenticate with only one method at a time — Microsoft Entra ID, AD DS, or Microsoft Entra Domain Services, never two simultaneously.
2. Enable Microsoft Entra Kerberos authentication on the storage account, which creates the Entra ID app registration backing the share.
3. Assign share-level permissions, either through default share-level permissions or Azure RBAC roles, then set the recommended NTFS-level permissions for the FSLogix profile folder.
4. Grant admin consent to the storage account's new service principal, and disable multifactor authentication on that service principal specifically — profile mounting happens silently at logon with no UX to complete step-up authentication, so an MFA-enforcing Conditional Access policy that catches this app breaks every profile load.
5. On the session host, enable the Kerberos/CloudKerberosTicketRetrievalEnabled setting via Intune Settings Catalog (now supported for Windows Enterprise multi-session) or Group Policy, then point FSLogix's VHDLocations registry value at the file share's UNC path.
6. For cloud-only or external identities specifically, also add the kdc_enable_cloud_group_sids tag to the app manifest so Entra includes cloud-only group SIDs in the Kerberos ticket.

Cloud-only and external identity support for this path is available in the Azure public cloud; hybrid identity support additionally covers Azure Government and the Azure operated by 21Vianet cloud.

## Licensing You Need Before You Start

Two license tracks matter here, and they're often conflated:

- **AVD access rights** — a per-user entitlement most organizations already own through Microsoft 365 E3/E5, Microsoft 365 Business Premium, or Windows Enterprise E3/E5; standalone per-user AVD access licenses exist for anyone who doesn't already qualify.
- **Microsoft Entra ID P1 (or P2)** — required for Conditional Access, dynamic device groups (used to hide the SSO consent prompt), and MFA enforcement. Don't assume this is bundled — verify it explicitly during planning, because everything in Lesson 2 depends on it.

## Turning On Microsoft Entra SSO for RDP

Microsoft's recommended remote-session authentication mechanism is Microsoft Entra SSO: it lets the connection skip the session host credential prompt entirely and sign the user in to Windows with a Microsoft Entra ID token, unlocking passwordless authentication and third-party identity provider federation inside the session too. Enabling it is five tasks:

1. **Enable Microsoft Entra authentication for RDP** — set isRemoteDesktopProtocolEnabled to true on the Windows Cloud Login service principal (app ID 270efc09-cd0d-444b-a71f-39af4910ec45), via the Azure portal (Microsoft Entra ID → Devices → Remote connection configuration) or the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK.
2. **Hide the consent prompt** — without this step, users see a "Yes, allow this connection" dialog the first time they hit a new host. Target a dynamic device group of your session hosts on the Windows Cloud Login service principal to suppress it.
3. **Create a Kerberos server object** — required if hosts are Entra hybrid joined, or if they're Entra joined but the environment still has AD DS domain controllers users need to reach.
4. **Review Conditional Access policies** — SSO introduces a new sign-in event at the session host, which Lesson 2 covers in depth.
5. **Enable SSO on the host pool** — set the RDP property Microsoft Entra single sign-on to "Connections will use Microsoft Entra authentication to provide single sign-on" in the portal, or set enablerdsaadauth to 1 via PowerShell.

Session hosts need Windows 11 (or Windows 10) Enterprise single or multi-session with the 2022-10 cumulative update or later, or Windows Server 2022 with its 2022-10 update, and must be Entra joined or Entra hybrid joined — Entra Domain Services-only or AD DS-only hosts are excluded from this feature entirely.

With identity and SSO wired up, Lesson 2 builds the access control layer on top: who gets which AVD role, and which Conditional Access apps actually govern each authentication phase.

slides.title: Identity for Azure Virtual Desktop
slides.sub: Join types, FSLogix Kerberos, and single sign-on
slides.narration: Welcome to Module 4, Identity and Security for Virtual Desktops. Everything in this module builds on one decision you make on day one: what identity backs your session hosts. In this lesson we cover the three ways to join a session host, the rule Azure Virtual Desktop never breaks about identity discoverability, how to run FSLogix profiles on Azure Files without a domain controller using Microsoft Entra Kerberos, and how to turn on Microsoft Entra single sign-on for RDP.

slides.title: Three Ways to Join a Session Host
bullets: Microsoft Entra joined: cloud-first, supports cloud-only users, no domain controller required
Microsoft Entra hybrid joined: preserves on-premises AD, supports hybrid users
Microsoft Entra Domain Services joined: lightweight managed domain, but no Entra SSO for RDP
AD DS joined with no Microsoft Entra ID presence: not supported at all
slides.narration: Azure Virtual Desktop supports three real join configurations. Microsoft Entra joined is the cloud-first option with no domain controller required. Microsoft Entra hybrid joined preserves your existing Active Directory footprint. Microsoft Entra Domain Services joined gives you a lightweight managed domain, but critically, it does not support Microsoft Entra single sign-on for RDP. And a session host joined only to standalone Active Directory, with no Microsoft Entra ID presence, is not a supported configuration at all.

slides.title: The Rule AVD Never Breaks
bullets: Users must be discoverable through Microsoft Entra ID, always
Standalone Active Directory-only identities are unsupported
AD FS federation without Entra ID sync is unsupported
Fix: Microsoft Entra Connect sync, or move to cloud-only accounts
slides.narration: There is one rule that never bends: every user identity accessing Azure Virtual Desktop must be discoverable through Microsoft Entra ID. A standalone Active Directory deployment, even one federated with AD FS, is not supported if it never synchronizes into Microsoft Entra ID. If you're migrating a legacy Remote Desktop Services estate that has never touched Entra ID, standing up Microsoft Entra Connect, or moving straight to cloud-only accounts, is where you start, not an optional cleanup step.

slides.title: Hybrid Identity's Sharp Edge
bullets: UPN mismatch between on-premises AD and Microsoft Entra ID is common
Supported only if the UPN or the SID matches across both directories
SID means AD ObjectSID matching Entra ID OnPremisesSecurityIdentifier
Symptom when it fails: portal sign-in works, desktop sign-in doesn't
slides.narration: Hybrid identity has a sharp edge that catches almost everyone eventually. Your on-premises account might be user at contoso dot local while Microsoft Entra ID knows the same person as user at contoso dot com. Azure Virtual Desktop only supports that mismatch if either the user principal name or the security identifier matches between the two directories. When neither matches, the classic symptom is that a user authenticates to the Azure Virtual Desktop service just fine but then fails to sign in to the session host itself.

slides.title: FSLogix Without a Domain Controller
bullets: Microsoft Entra Kerberos lets Entra ID issue SMB Kerberos tickets directly
Hybrid or Entra-joined hosts skip domain controller line-of-sight at logon
A storage account can use only one authentication method at a time
Cloud-only and external identity support is limited to the Azure public cloud
slides.narration: Historically, FSLogix profiles on Azure Files needed a domain controller in the network path at every logon. Microsoft Entra Kerberos changes that: Microsoft Entra ID itself issues the Kerberos tickets needed to reach the file share over standard SMB, so hybrid-joined or Entra-joined session hosts don't need line-of-sight to a domain controller to load a profile. One constraint to remember: a storage account can only authenticate with one method at a time, Microsoft Entra ID, Active Directory, or Microsoft Entra Domain Services, never two together.

slides.title: Configuring Entra Kerberos for FSLogix
bullets: Enable Microsoft Entra Kerberos on the storage account
Assign share-level and NTFS-level permissions for the profile folder
Grant admin consent, then disable MFA on the storage account's service principal
Enable CloudKerberosTicketRetrievalEnabled via Intune Settings Catalog or Group Policy
slides.narration: The configuration runs in a defined order. First, enable Microsoft Entra Kerberos on the storage account, which creates its Entra ID app registration. Then assign share-level and NTFS permissions for the profile folder. Next, grant admin consent to the new service principal and disable multifactor authentication specifically on that service principal, because profile mounting happens silently at logon with no way to complete a step-up prompt. Finally, turn on the CloudKerberosTicketRetrievalEnabled setting on the session host through Intune's Settings Catalog or Group Policy.

slides.title: Licensing Before You Start
bullets: AVD access rights via Microsoft 365 E3/E5, Business Premium, or a standalone license
Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 required for Conditional Access and dynamic groups
Don't assume P1 is bundled — verify it explicitly during planning
License gaps here block everything covered in Lesson 2
slides.narration: Two license tracks matter and people conflate them constantly. AVD access rights typically come bundled through Microsoft 365 E3 or E5, Business Premium, or Windows Enterprise E3 or E5, with standalone per-user licenses available otherwise. Separately, Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 is required for Conditional Access, dynamic groups, and multifactor authentication enforcement. Never assume P1 is already included, verify it explicitly, because the access control lesson that follows this one depends entirely on it.

slides.title: Turning On Microsoft Entra SSO for RDP
bullets: Enable Entra authentication for RDP on the Windows Cloud Login app
Hide the consent prompt using a dynamic device group
Create a Kerberos server object when hybrid joined or reaching on-prem resources
Enable SSO on the host pool with enablerdsaadauth
slides.narration: Turning on single sign-on is five tasks. Enable Microsoft Entra authentication for RDP on the Windows Cloud Login application. Hide the consent prompt by targeting a dynamic device group of your session hosts. Create a Kerberos server object if your hosts are hybrid joined or need to reach on-premises resources. Review your Conditional Access policies, which we cover next lesson. And finally enable single sign-on on the host pool itself, either through the portal or by setting enablerdsaadauth to one in PowerShell.

slides.title: SSO Prerequisites
bullets: Entra joined or Entra hybrid joined hosts only
Windows 11 or 10 Enterprise with the 2022-10 cumulative update or later
Windows Server 2022 with its 2022-10 update also qualifies
Entra Domain Services-only and AD DS-only hosts are excluded
slides.narration: Before you flip the switch, check the prerequisites. Session hosts must be Microsoft Entra joined or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined. They need Windows 11 or Windows 10 Enterprise, single or multi-session, with the October 2022 cumulative update or later, or Windows Server 2022 with its equivalent update. Hosts joined only to Microsoft Entra Domain Services or only to standalone Active Directory are excluded from this feature no matter what update level they're running.

slides.title: Where This Leads
bullets: Identity choice determines every later security control in this module
SSO introduces a second Microsoft Entra sign-in event at the session host
Lesson 2 covers RBAC roles and Conditional Access app targeting
Lesson 3 layers Intune and Defender for Endpoint hardening on top
slides.narration: Everything you decide in this lesson ripples forward. Enabling single sign-on introduces a second Microsoft Entra sign-in event, one at the service and one at the session host, and that second event is exactly what the next lesson's Conditional Access policies need to target correctly. From there we move to role-based access control and Conditional Access app targeting, then to Intune and Defender for Endpoint hardening on the session hosts themselves.
